description: I am an independent participant who is interested in space exploration, science, creativity, and learning new things. I enjoy sharing ideas and discovering innovative ways to understand our universe. I welcome participants who are interested in planets, space exploration, research, and graphic design.
summary: This project presents a visual poster about identifying Earth locations that share similarities with the Moon and Mars. It illustrates Earth, the Moon, Mars, and space exploration vehicles to show the connection between our planet and other celestial bodies. The poster highlights the importance of studying Earth's different environments to better understand the surfaces of the Moon and Mars. This project aims to encourage curiosity about space exploration and show how studying places on Earth can help scientists prepare for future space missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Our project addresses the challenge of identifying optimal Earth analog locations that replicate the extreme environmental conditions of permanent Lunar bases and Mars. Through a structured visual design and infographic poster, we compare key planetary parameters—such as terrain topography, volcanic geology, extreme temperatures, and arid conditions—between extraterrestrial targets and selected Earth locations. This serves as an intuitive visual guide for identifying high-fidelity testing grounds for future space habitats, rovers, and astronaut training. Key Factors Considered: Our team carefully evaluated multiple scientific and practical criteria, including geological similarity (such as basaltic plains, lava tubes, and impact craters), regolith composition, extreme climate isolation, and logistical accessibility for research teams to conduct field simulations. Benefits & Intended Impact: Testing space technologies directly on the Moon or Mars is extremely costly and high-risk. Our visual design helps researchers, students, and space enthusiasts easily understand where and how space agencies can test life-support systems and robotics right here on Earth. By making complex planetary data visually accessible, our project raises public awareness and supports mission planning to reduce risks and accelerate humanity's sustainable return to the Moon and journey to Mars. Creativity & Tools Used: To turn complex planetary science into an engaging and easy-to-digest experience, we combined scientific research with visual storytelling and clean graphic layout design. We utilized NASA's open-source planetary exploration data for our research, and used graphic design software to create our original design drafts, comparative visuals, and presentation layouts.

No Super Intelligence (SI) or AI tools were used in the creation of this project. All research, data analysis, text, and visual design drafts were created entirely by our team.
